summary_title: Customer Churn Prediction & Probability Calibration Improvement Summary

dataset.name: churn_training_data.csv
dataset.provenance: Synthetic platform customer transaction and engagement profiles
dataset.caveat: Evaluated on synthetic platform accounts. Results validate probability calibration methods but cannot be generalized as empirical customer behavior.

experimental_protocol.selection_criterion: Predefined validation ROC-AUC on development fold
experimental_protocol.calibration_protocol: Platt sigmoid scaling fitted strictly on out-of-fold validation margins; zero leakage into test set
experimental_protocol.binning_method: 10-bin equal-width Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier score

key_findings: Calibrated LinearSVC reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE) from 0.0434 (Random Forest) to 0.0315 (-27.4% relative error reduction) while achieving highest 5-seed ROC-AUC (0.8169).
Logistic Regression achieves robust linear discrimination (ROC-AUC 0.8167 +- 0.0103, F1 0.7259 +- 0.0132) with low computational training latency (0.188s vs 0.787s for Random Forest).
All churn results reflect synthetic platform customer records because Indian retail POS registers lack continuous customer tracking identifiers; claims of real customer retention remain unsupported.
